_README: LifeLine demo CUSTOMER POLICY RECORDS -- FICTIONAL HACKATHON DATA.
These represent an INDIVIDUAL customer's existing policy (their actual
coverage amount, duration, the benefits and riders THEY hold, and their
specific limitations). This is deliberately separate from the PRODUCT
catalog in demo_policies.json, which only describes what a product is.
- Every record here is FICTIONAL demo data. There is NO real customer data
in this repo and NO code path that reaches a real policy-administration
system. A policy number alone must never surface a real person's record;
this service only ever returns these clearly-labelled demo records.
- Demo record IDs use the strict prefix 'DEMO-' precisely so that a bare
numeric policy number (e.g. '100000123') cannot match anything. Only a
recognised demo ID resolves; everything else is treated as unknown.
- A record states the riders the holder ACTUALLY has. Never assume a holder
carries every optional rider the product catalog lists.
Each record links to its PRODUCT via product_id (into demo_policies.json)
and to a sample policy DOCUMENT (repo markdown + page/section, and an S3
key for a future presigned-URL hand-off). No URLs or credentials here.

_field_notes.id: Strict demo id, always prefixed 'DEMO-'. This is the only form the lookup accepts.
_field_notes.product_id: Links to the product catalog entry (demo_policies.json) this policy is based on.
_field_notes.coverage_amount: The holder's actual death benefit for THIS policy (fictional demo figure).
_field_notes.riders_held: ONLY the optional riders this holder actually has. May be empty. Never inferred from the product catalog.
_field_notes.document: Sample policy document reference: repo markdown source + page/section, plus S3 bucket/key for a future presigned URL.

records.demo_disclaimer: Hackathon Demo — Fictional sample policy record, not a real customer's policy.
benefits_included: Death benefit of $250,000 paid to the named beneficiary if the insured dies during the 20-year term.
limitations: Coverage ends at the end of the 20-year term (2041); there is no payout if the insured outlives the term.
This term policy builds no cash value.
A beneficiary must be named and kept current for the death benefit to be paid as intended.

benefits_included: Death benefit of $500,000 paid to the named beneficiary if the insured dies during the 30-year term.

riders_held.name: Waiver of premium rider
riders_held.plain_language: If the insured becomes totally disabled, future premiums are waived while the disability continues, so the coverage stays in force.

limitations: Coverage ends at the end of the 30-year term (2049); there is no payout if the insured outlives the term.
This term policy builds no cash value.
Rider terms (such as the waiver of premium) have their own conditions that apply only while those conditions are met.

records.coverage_duration: Permanent; may continue for life while the policy is kept in force
benefits_included: Death benefit of $300,000 paid to the named beneficiary.
Potential cash-value growth linked to an index methodology (not a direct index investment; growth is not guaranteed).
limitations: Lifetime coverage is not unconditional; it depends on the policy being kept in force (sufficient premium and cash value).
Cash-value growth is index-linked and not guaranteed; it may underperform expectations.
This is a more complex policy than term insurance.
